S04.item: Dr. Trimen's Typical Ledgeriana Tree (letter of Walter Agar, Lawrence, June 22nd, 1883)

S03.item: Dr. Trimen's Ledgeriana: Mr. T. N. Christie to the Rescue (letter, St. Andrew's, Maskeliya, 7th June 1883)

meta.note: Local record identifiers only. No Wikidata or other authority identifiers. Columns beginning 'inferred_' and 'outside_identification' are NOT stated by the sources.

records.printed_text: DR. TRIMEN'S TYPICAL LEDGERIANA TREE. … The tree, which was sketched for Dr. Trimen's work, is dead.
records.stated_detail: Named in the title; a tree was sketched for 'Dr. Trimen's work'; was with Mr. Moens when the trees were seen at Mahanillu estate.
records.inferred_same_as: S03-P02 (probable: same surname, title and subject)

records.printed_text: We publish below a letter from Mr. Agar … Lawrence, June 22nd, 1883. … WALTER AGAR.
records.stated_detail: Writer of the letter; full forename 'Walter' is given in the signature.
records.inferred_same_as: S03-P04 (probable: S03 prints only 'Mr. Agar', planter of the plant at Mahanilu)

records.printed_text: Mr. Howard himself having given testimony to that effect after having analyzed the bark … to Mr. Howard, who pronounced it to be Ledgeriana bark
records.stated_detail: Analysed the bark and pronounced it Ledgeriana bark.
records.inferred_same_as: S03-P01 (probable: S03 prints 'Mr. J. E. Howard'; S04 gives no initials)
records.inferred_note: Initials 'J. E.' are NOT supplied here because S04 does not print them.

records.printed_text: I have little to add to what Mr. Christie has written on the subject of Ledgerianas
records.stated_detail: Has written on the subject of Ledgerianas.
records.inferred_same_as: S03-P09 (probable: S03 is a letter on Ledgerianas signed THOS. NORTH CHRISTIE, one week to 'June 7th'; S04 does not say which item is meant)
records.inferred_note: Link to S03 rests on subject matter and date; S04 does not name the piece Mr. Christie wrote.

records.printed_text: one of several Mr. Moens saw in flower at Mahanillu estate, Dr. Trimen was with Mr. Moens
records.stated_detail: Saw several trees in flower; agreed with Dr. Trimen they were true Ledgerianas; had sent 'the other' (see S04-T03).

records.printed_text: sent home by Mr. Campbell for analysis to Mr. Howard
records.stated_detail: Sent the bark of some of the trees home for analysis.
records.inferred_same_as: S03-P07 (probable: S03 prints 'Mr. J. A. Campbell of Lindula, Ceylon'; S04 gives only 'Mr. Campbell')

records.printed_text: —Ed.]
records.stated_detail: Editorial note introducing the letter; no personal name printed.
records.reading_note: Kept as an unnamed role-record (editor of the journal); it is not a personal name. Drop if only named people are wanted.
records.inferred_note: That 'Ed.' is the journal's editor is the conventional reading of the abbreviation.

records.printed_text: the tree figured by Dr. Trimen was an undoubted Ledgeriana … The tree, which was sketched for Dr. Trimen's work, is dead. … It was one of several Mr. Moens saw in flower at Mahanillu estate
records.printed_name: the tree, which was sketched for Dr. Trimen's work
records.stated_detail: Called 'an undoubted Ledgeriana' (editor) and 'typical' (title); 'is dead'; one of several trees Mr. Moens saw in flower at Mahanillu estate.
records.inferred_same_as: S03-T01 (probable: 'The plant which Dr. Trimen figured', planted on Mahanilu by Mr. Agar)
records.inferred_note: 'It' in 'It was one of several...' is read as the sketched tree. 'sketched' (S04) vs 'figured' (S03) are taken as the same illustration; the texts do not say so.

records.printed_text: The trees were only about 4½ years old from the time the plants were put out, and were now in a full condition and in flower.
records.printed_name: these trees (the several seen in flower)
records.date_or_age_as_printed: about 4½ years old from the time the plants were put out
records.stated_detail: Agreed by Dr. Trimen and Mr. Moens to be true Ledgerianas; in flower.
records.reading_note: 'in a full condition' may be an OCR or printing slip (e.g. 'in full bloom'); transcribed as printed. Place 'Mahanillu estate' is stated for the first sentence and carried here by 'these trees'.

records.printed_text: as well as the other that Mr. Moens had sent to be true Ledgerianas
records.printed_name: the other [that Mr. Moens had sent]
records.stated_detail: Something Mr. Moens 'had sent to be true Ledgerianas', named alongside the leaf prints ('as well as the other').
records.reading_note: Sentence is garbled: 'the other' lacks its noun (tree? leaves? plant?) and 'sent to be true Ledgerianas' may be missing words (e.g. 'sent, said to be'). Not interpreted.
records.inferred_note: Treated as a plant/material item only because the sentence concerns leaf prints of trees.

records.printed_text: The bark of some of these trees was sent home by Mr. Campbell for analysis to Mr. Howard, who pronounced it to be Ledgeriana bark, giving 7 per cent of pure quinine (equal I believe to 9 of sulphate) and only a trace of other alkaloids.
records.printed_name: The bark of some of these trees
records.stated_detail: Sent home by Mr. Campbell to Mr. Howard for analysis; pronounced Ledgeriana bark; '7 per cent of pure quinine'; 'only a trace of other alkaloids'; '(equal I believe to 9 of sulphate)' is the writer's belief, not a measured value.
records.inferred_note: Which trees supplied the bark is not stated beyond 'some of these trees'; whether it includes S04-T01 is not said.

records.printed_text: I have by my prints of the leaves of some of the trees
records.printed_name: prints of the leaves of some of the trees
records.stated_detail: In the writer's keeping 'so that it will be easy in the future to determine the question'.
records.reading_note: 'I have by my prints' is probably 'I have by me prints' (OCR/print slip); transcribed as printed.

records.printed_text: I have also in my possession the bark from the tree itself, but taken when it was dying.
records.printed_name: the bark from the tree itself
records.stated_detail: Bark taken when the tree was dying; in the writer's possession.
records.inferred_same_as: S04-T01 is the tree (probable: 'the tree itself' follows the discussion of the sketched tree)
records.inferred_note: 'the tree itself' is read as the sketched tree of S04-T01, not one of the other trees.

records.printed_text: We publish below a letter from Mr. Agar
records.stated_detail: The editor publishes a letter from Mr. Agar.

records.printed_text: which places beyond question the fact that the tree figured by Dr. Trimen was an undoubted Ledgeriana
records.stated_detail: Editor's claim about the letter's effect; subject is the letter itself.
records.verb_as_printed: places beyond question the fact that ... was an undoubted Ledgeriana
records.inferred_note: subject_id left blank because the grammatical subject is the letter, not a person.

records.printed_text: I have little to add to what Mr. Christie has written on the subject of Ledgerianas
records.verb_as_printed: have little to add to what ... has written

records.printed_text: The tree, which was sketched for Dr. Trimen's work
records.stated_detail: Object is 'Dr. Trimen's work' (a publication), recorded against Dr. Trimen; the person who sketched it is not named.
records.inferred_note: The work is not named or described beyond 'Dr. Trimen's work'; S03 mentions 'Dr. Trimen's description and figure of C. ledgeriana' but the link is not stated.

records.printed_text: several Mr. Moens saw in flower at Mahanillu estate
It was one of several Mr. Moens saw in flower
Dr. Trimen was with Mr. Moens
both agreed the trees were true Ledgerianas
The bark of some of these trees was sent home by Mr. Campbell for analysis to Mr. Howard
Mr. Howard, who pronounced it to be Ledgeriana bark
records.verb_as_printed: pronounced it to be Ledgeriana bark

records.printed_text: Mr. Howard himself having given testimony to that effect after having analyzed the bark
records.verb_as_printed: having given testimony ... after having analyzed

records.printed_text: the other that Mr. Moens had sent to be true Ledgerianas
records.verb_as_printed: had sent to be true Ledgerianas

records.printed_text: I have by my prints of the leaves of some of the trees
I have also in my possession the bark from the tree itself
Were the question raised by Mr. J. E. Howard purely technical … communicated to Mr. J. E. Howard, F. R. S., who raised seedlings
records.stated_detail: Raised the question; raised seedlings from Java seed (Kew report); author of 'Mr. Howard's latest paper' and 'Howard's great work'; characterised by the writer as having 'the knowledge of hot-house plants and dried specimens'.

records.printed_text: Dr. Trimen's description and figure of *C. ledgeriana* … Dr. Trimen, who has seen the Ceylon and Indian plantations, and many mature analyzed trees, knows and has figured *C. Ledgeriana*
records.stated_detail: Described and figured C. ledgeriana; selected a tree for specimens; has 'seen the Ceylon and Indian plantations, and many mature analyzed trees'.

records.printed_text: raised from McIvor's seed by me
records.stated_detail: Source of the seed from which the figured plant was raised (as printed, 'McIvor's seed'); no title or forename printed.
records.inferred_note: Printed without title or initials; not expanded.

records.printed_text: planted on Mahanilu by Mr. Agar
records.stated_detail: Planted the figured plant on Mahanilu.

records.printed_text: its descent from Ledger's original seed is undoubted
records.stated_detail: 'Ledger's original seed' is the stated origin of the figured plant's line.
records.inferred_note: Printed as 'Ledger' only; no forename or title; not expanded. The plant name 'Ledgeriana' is, by common usage, derived from this name, but the text does not say so.

records.printed_text: Mr. T. Christy's Bolivian calisaya seedlings
records.stated_detail: Owner of 'Bolivian calisaya seedlings'; spelled 'Christy' (not 'Christie').
records.inferred_note: Spelling 'Christy' differs from 'Christie' (the letter-writer); treated as a different person; not expanded.

records.printed_text: Mr. J. A. Campbell of Lindula, Ceylon, who was anxious to have a perfectly authentic strain
records.stated_detail: Received three rooted cuttings; wrote to the letter-writer on 5th instant; quoted at length.

records.printed_text: according to Mr. Moens' idea of one … Moens' identification of Dr. Trimen's plant
records.stated_detail: Has an 'idea' of a pure-type Ledgeriana tree; identified Dr. Trimen's plant; forwarded seed to Mr. Howard; the writer asks 'why should the infallibility of Moens be relied on'.

records.printed_text: MR. T. N. CHRISTIE TO THE RESCUE. … St. Andrew's, Maskeliya, 7th June 1883. … THOS. NORTH CHRISTIE.
records.printed_name: THOS. NORTH CHRISTIE (signature); MR. T. N. CHRISTIE (title)
records.stated_detail: Letter-writer; says he raised plants from McIvor's seed ('by me').
records.inferred_note: First-person 'I'/'me'/'my' throughout S03 is read as this person, because the letter is signed by him.

records.printed_text: The plant which Dr. Trimen figured was one of those raised from McIvor's seed by me, and planted on Mahanilu by Mr. Agar, and its descent from Ledger's original seed is undoubted.
records.printed_name: The plant which Dr. Trimen figured
records.stated_detail: One of those raised from McIvor's seed by the writer; planted on Mahanilu by Mr. Agar; descent from Ledger's original seed 'undoubted'; also called 'the Ledger figured by Dr. Trimen' and 'his figured type'.

records.printed_text: Other plants, exactly similar in blossom, raised from the same pinch of seed, have given over 12, 13 and 14 per cent sulphate of quinine
records.printed_name: Other plants, exactly similar in blossom, raised from the same pinch of seed
records.stated_detail: Analyses 'over 12, 13 and 14 per cent sulphate of quinine'.
records.inferred_note: 'the same pinch of seed' is read as the seed that produced S03-T01; the three analyses are not tied to individual plants or dates.

records.printed_text: the very trees which Mr. Howard called in to help him, the Yarrow Ledgers, have the same blossom, and came out of the same nursery bed as the Ledger figured by Dr. Trimen!
records.stated_detail: Called in by Mr. Howard 'to help him'; 'have the same blossom'; 'came out of the same nursery bed'.
records.inferred_note: 'Yarrow' appears to be a place or owner's name but the text does not say.

records.printed_text: Dr. Trimen selected a tree here for specimens, as being botanically a typical Ledger, and his selection was well borne out, when, on the following day, the analysis of that very tree arrived from England and showed 11.29 S.
records.stated_detail: Selected 'as being botanically a typical Ledger'; its analysis 'showed 11.29 S.' (analysis arrived the following day).
records.inferred_note: 'here' is read as the place named in the dateline (St. Andrew's, Maskeliya). 'S.' is read as sulphate of quinine; the text does not spell this out. Percentage unit not printed.

records.printed_text: When Mr. Howard goes on to identify by these characteristics Mr. T. Christy's Bolivian calisaya seedlings as true Ledgerianas … I have some of Mr. T. Christy's Bolivian plants, 18 months old, and I most certainly say they are not Ledgers. They seem to be Calisayas of some kind
records.printed_name: Mr. T. Christy's Bolivian calisaya seedlings
records.stated_detail: Identified by Mr. Howard as true Ledgerianas; the writer says they 'are not Ledgers' and 'seem to be Calisayas of some kind'; the writer has some.
records.inferred_note: 'seedlings' and 'plants' are read as the same stock (the second sentence says 'some of ... plants').

records.printed_text: Dr. Trimen's illustration of the blossom (but not of the tree itself) is particularly good, a contrast to that given in Howard's great work, where the figured plant is far from being a typical Ledgeriana, if indeed it is one at all.
records.printed_name: the figured plant [in Howard's great work]
records.date_or_age_as_printed: written '9 months ago, in the Dikoya essay'
records.stated_detail: Quoted from the writer's own earlier essay; the plant figured is 'far from being a typical Ledgeriana, if indeed it is one at all'.
records.inferred_note: Also referred to as 'Mr. Howard's figured "Ledgeriana"' (line 5), read as the same figured plant. Title of Howard's 'great work' not printed.

records.printed_text: the misunderstanding which arose about the Annfield and Emelina Calisayas, some two years ago
records.stated_detail: Subject of a 'misunderstanding'; 'most of these Calisayas seemed exactly similar to Mr. Howard's figured "Ledgeriana"'.
records.inferred_note: 'Annfield' and 'Emelina' read as the names of two Calisaya stocks (or places); text does not say.

records.printed_text: In 1876, some seed was received at Kew from Java, and part of this was communicated to Mr. J. E. Howard, F. R. S., who raised seedlings.
records.printed_name: some seed [received at Kew from Java]
records.stated_detail: Part of it communicated to Mr. J. E. Howard. Elsewhere (line 15) the writer says Mr. Howard 'wishes to believe' that 'the first seed received at Kew was genuine'.
records.asserted_by: Kew Gardens Report for 1880, p. 12 (as quoted by S03-P09)

records.printed_text: who raised seedlings. He carefully selected the most promising of these, … very kindly supplied Kew with cuttings both of the figured and of another selected plant in the course of last year.
records.printed_name: the figured [plant] and another selected plant
records.date_or_age_as_printed: 'in the course of last year' (relative to the 1880 Report)
records.stated_detail: Cuttings of 'both the figured and ... another selected plant' were supplied to Kew.
records.asserted_by: Kew Gardens Report for 1880, p. 12 (as quoted by S03-P09)
records.inferred_note: 'last year' is relative to the Report, so the calendar year is not printed; it would be 1879 if the Report year is the publication year, but this is NOT stated. 'the figured' [plant] presumably = S03-T06.

records.printed_text: Three of the rooted cuttings were given to Mr. J. A. Campbell of Lindula, Ceylon, who was anxious to have a perfectly authentic strain.
records.stated_detail: Given to Mr. J. A. Campbell, 'anxious to have a perfectly authentic strain'.
records.asserted_by: Kew Gardens Report for 1880, p. 12 (as quoted by S03-P09)

records.printed_text: Three other plants, imported at Kew from the same authentic strain were sent to Jamaica.
records.printed_name: Three other plants, imported at Kew from the same authentic strain
records.stated_detail: Sent to Jamaica.
records.asserted_by: Kew Gardens Report for 1880, p. 12 (as quoted by S03-P09)
records.reading_note: The paragraph heading is printed '*Indonesia*.—' but the content concerns Jamaica; probably a misprint or OCR error for 'Jamaica.'. Heading transcribed as printed; location taken from the sentence.

records.printed_text: those "authentic" cuttings, which I have seen in the Waltrim clearing, are not Ledgerianas at all
records.stated_detail: Writer says they 'are not Ledgerianas at all'.
records.inferred_same_as: S03-T10 (probable: 'authentic' cuttings from Mr. Howard to Mr. Campbell)
records.inferred_note: The 'Waltrim clearing' is not said to be Mr. Campbell's, though Campbell's trees are discussed in the next sentence; ownership is inferred only.

records.printed_text: the trees I have (raised from cuttings received from Mr. Howard) Ledgerianas. Two of them are very shrubby in their growth, and with hard shiny leaves. The other is a Calisaya of the broad-leaved variety, very much like what I believe is called in Java *Calisaya Anglica*.
records.printed_name: the trees I have (raised from cuttings received from Mr. Howard)
records.stated_detail: Two 'very shrubby in their growth, and with hard shiny leaves'; the other 'a Calisaya of the broad-leaved variety'.
records.asserted_by: P07 (quoted letter of 5th instant, as quoted by S03-P09)
records.reading_note: Span is a trimmed excerpt that begins mid-sentence ('...would think of calling the trees I have (...) Ledgerianas.').
records.inferred_note: The count of three is inferred from 'Two of them ... The other' and from the earlier 'Three of the rooted cuttings'. 'I' in the quotation is Mr. Campbell (quoted letter), not the letter-writer.

records.printed_text: I have also another plant that Mr. Howard kindly gave me which I understood him to say had been raised from Ledgeriana seed received from Java. This is the best, so far as appearance goes, but I should not call it a Ledgeriana.
records.printed_name: another plant that Mr. Howard kindly gave me
records.stated_detail: Said (as understood) to be raised from Ledgeriana seed received from Java; 'the best, so far as appearance goes'; 'I should not call it a Ledgeriana'.
records.asserted_by: P07 (quoted letter of 5th instant, as quoted by S03-P09)

records.printed_text: Ledger's original seed
records.stated_detail: Stated origin of the figured plant's descent.

records.printed_text: raised from McIvor's seed by me … the same pinch of seed
records.printed_name: McIvor's seed ('the same pinch of seed')
records.stated_detail: Seed from which the figured plant and 'other plants' were raised.
records.inferred_note: 'the same pinch of seed' is read as McIvor's seed; relation of McIvor's seed to Ledger's original seed is not stated beyond 'descent'.

records.printed_text: he asserts that other seed forwarded to him by Mr. Moens as true Ledgeriana turned out to be nothing of the kind
records.printed_name: other seed forwarded to him by Mr. Moens
records.stated_detail: Mr. Howard 'asserts' it was not true Ledgeriana.

records.printed_text: the analysis of that very tree arrived from England and showed 11.29 S.
records.printed_name: the analysis of that very tree
records.stated_detail: Arrived from England on the day after Dr. Trimen selected the tree; 'showed 11.29 S.'.
records.inferred_note: Whether bark was analysed is not stated here. 'S.' read as sulphate of quinine (unit not spelled out).
